32. Logical issue: `should_use_web_search` uses substring checks like `if kw in message_lower`, so a word like `"newton"` will trigger `"new"` and incorrectly decide to use web search.[1]

43. Logical issue: `/api/upload` reads the entire file into memory with `file_data = await file.read()`; very large uploads will increase memory usage significantly and may exceed limits.[1]

44. Logical issue: `/api/upload` attempts to decode text files as UTF‑8 with `errors="ignore"`, which can silently drop characters and lead to incomplete `text_content`.[1]

45. Logical issue: `/api/upload` stores the entire file binary blob in `LONGBLOB` and entire decoded content in `LONGTEXT` with no size checks; this may make the database grow very quickly for large or many files.[1]

46. Logical issue: `get_messages` only checks that a conversation with that id and user_id exists, but does not enforce pagination; for long conversations, returning all messages in one response may be slow and heavy.[1]

47. Logical issue: `list_conversations` returns all conversations for a user without pagination or limit; many conversations will lead to large responses.[1]

48. Logical issue: `delete_conversation` deletes only from the `conversations` table but does not cascade delete `messages` or `uploaded_files` referencing that conversation unless foreign keys with `ON DELETE CASCADE` exist at the DB level, which are not defined here.[1]

49. Logical issue: `rename_conversation` updates only `title` but not `updated_at`; although MySQL’s `ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` is defined, if the schema or database flavor changes, this assumption might break.[1]

50. Logical issue: during registration, the email and username uniqueness rely on database constraints; the code catches `pymysql.err.IntegrityError` but does not differentiate between which field caused the conflict.[1]

51. Logical issue: login uses `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = %s`; this assumes emails are unique but that uniqueness is not programmatically asserted except by DB constraint.[1]

52. Logical issue: `get_current_user` expects `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header exactly; any token provided via cookie or query parameter is ignored, which may not align with some frontend patterns.[1]

53. Logical issue: when JWT decoding fails in `decode_token`, the function returns a 401 for any exception, including malformed tokens and system errors, which may hide internal problems like wrong `JWT_SECRET`.[1]

54. Logical issue: `app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=".", html=True), name="static")` serves the entire project directory, which may expose source code and config files if placed in that directory structure.[1]

55. Logical issue: `allow_origins=["*"]` and `allow_credentials=True` on CORS middleware is an invalid combination by browser rules; browsers will reject credentialed requests with wildcard origin, so this configuration is self‑contradictory.[1]

56. Logical issue: several string literals in SQL statements use hardcoded table names and column lists; if the DB schema changes, all of these statements must be updated manually, which is error‑prone.[1]

57. Logical issue: `run_exa_search` builds bullet summaries like `"- {title}: {summary}"` but does not escape newline characters, so summaries containing newlines will break formatting and potentially confuse the LLM.[1]

58. Logical issue: `build_exa_query_params` hardcodes `"type": "instant"`, which assumes this search type exists and remains stable in the Exa API.[1]

59. Logical issue: `generate_image_from_prompt` sets `"aspect_ratio": None` and `"image_size": None` in payload; if the API does not accept `None` for those fields, the call will fail.[1]

60. Logical issue: in `/api/chat`, the system message `"You are a helpful, intelligent assistant. Answer in the same language the user writes in. Be concise and accurate."` may conflict with user preferences for verbosity or style but is hardcoded.[1]

61. Logical issue: `/api/chat` does not include any explicit guardrails on `req.message` size; extremely long inputs could exceed the model or server limits and cause errors.[1]

62. Logical issue: `/api/chat` calls `openai_client.chat.completions.create` with `model="zai-org/GLM-5"`; if this model is not available in the configured OpenAI endpoint, the call will fail.[1]

63. Logical issue: `/api/chat` does not handle non‑200 responses or API errors from the OpenAI client explicitly; any exception will bubble up as a 500 internal server error.[1]

64. Logical issue: `exa_client = Exa(EXA_API_KEY)` is constructed at import time; if the key is invalid or network unreachable, application startup will fail.[1]

65. Logical issue: `init_db()` is called at import time and wrapped in a broad `except Exception as e`, printing only a warning; real DB schema issues might go unnoticed because the app continues running even if tables are missing.[1]

66. Logical issue: `get_db()` yields a new connection per request but does not implement connection pooling; under load, this may open many simultaneous connections to the DB.[1]

67. Logical issue: `ssl={"ssl": {}}` configuration for MySQL is very minimal and assumes default SSL handling; if the DB requires specific certificates, this will fail.[1]

68. Logical issue: `uploaded_files.conversation_id` is nullable, but `/api/upload` does not validate that the provided `conversation_id` belongs to the `user_id`, so files might be attached to arbitrary conversations if IDs are guessed (assuming syntax and foreign keys corrected).[1]

69. Logical issue: the `uploaded_files` table has no index on `user_id` or `conversation_id` beyond the primary key on `id`; queries filtering by these may be slower as data grows.[1]

70. Logical issue: the `messages` table has no index on `conversation_id` other than implicit primary key index on `id`; fetching messages by conversation could degrade in performance.[1]

71. Logical issue: the `conversations` table has no explicit index on `user_id`, so queries that filter and order by `user_id` and `updated_at` may be slower on large datasets.[1]

72. Logical issue: some Hungarian keywords in `news_keywords` and recency detection are duplicated semantically or partially overlapping, which may make behavior inconsistent between languages.[1]

73. Logical issue: when `run_exa_search` builds `summaries` and `sources`, it does not de‑duplicate results; if Exa returns near duplicates, multiple very similar entries will be injected into the context.[1]

74. Logical issue: `exa_sources` stored in `messages` for assistant messages uses the results from the *current* chat call only; previous web search sources are not recalled for future use.[1]

75. Logical issue: `ChatRequest.file_ids` default is `[]` at class definition time; using a mutable default in pydantic models is generally discouraged because of shared state, though pydantic typically handles this by model parsing.[1]

76. Logical issue: `NewConversationRequest.title` default is `"New Chat"`, but when `/api/chat` auto‑creates a conversation, it sets title to the first 60 characters of the message instead, leading to differing behaviors depending on which endpoint is used.[1]

77. Logical issue: `/api/chat` does not update the conversation title when the user continues the conversation, even if the initial title is not descriptive.[1]

78. Logical issue: `app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=".", html=True), name="static")` at the end means any unmatched path is served as static content, which may shadow or conflict with intended API routes if not configured carefully.[1]

79. Logical issue: `/api/me` returns `user` which likely contains `created_at` as a `datetime` object; timezone handling is not explicit and relies on DB defaults.[1]

80. Logical issue: registering a new user with the same email but different letter case may or may not be allowed depending on DB collation; the code does not normalize case.[1]

81. Logical issue: login queries by email without normalizing or lowercasing, so `User@example.com` and `user@example.com` may be treated differently.[1]

82. Logical issue: password field `password_hash VARCHAR(255)` assumes bcrypt hashes will always fit; if a different hashing scheme is used later, it might not.[1]

83. Logical issue: the `messages` table stores `reasoning_content` and `exa_sources` as `TEXT`; large reasoning traces and many sources could exceed default row size limits depending on DB configuration.[1]

84. Logical issue: in `/api/chat`, `history = cur.fetchall()` retrieves all messages for the conversation each time; for long histories this is inefficient if only the last 20 are used.[1]

85. Logical issue: `should_use_web_search` includes year strings `"2024"`, `"2025"`, `"2026"`; as time passes, these will become outdated and fail to trigger search for newer years.[1]

86. Logical issue: `build_exa_query_params` sets the time window to the last 90 days; for certain use cases, this may be too short and miss relevant content, or too long and include stale content.[1]

87. Logical issue: `/api/upload` does not constrain allowed MIME types beyond simple substring checking, so binary files with misleading extensions may be misclassified.[1]

88. Logical issue: `/api/chat` does not explicitly include system prompt or conversation metadata in database; clients cannot reconstruct the full reasoning context that the model saw.[1]

89. Logical issue: there is no `/health` or similar endpoint to check DB, Exa, and OpenAI health, so monitoring is limited.[1]

90. Logical issue: there is no rate limiting or abuse protection at the application level, so automated clients could spam `/api/chat` or `/api/upload`.[1]

91. Logical issue: `get_messages` sorts by `created_at ASC`; if two messages share exact same timestamp, order relies on DB implementation.[1]

92. Logical issue: datetime fields rely on DB side `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`; no timezone conversion occurs at application layer, which may cause ambiguity if DB is not in UTC.[1]

93. Logical issue: if `run_exa_search` raises any exception other than `FlyMyAIPredictException`, it is not caught; `/api/chat` will fail with 500 on such errors.[1]

94. Logical issue: `generate_image_from_prompt` catches only `FlyMyAIPredictException` and not generic exceptions like `ValueError` from base64 decoding, leading to possible 500s.[1]

95. Logical issue: `should_use_web_search` and `detect_image_request` operate independently; if a user asks for an image of a very recent event, both may trigger, but the behavior is not specifically tailored for such combinations.[1]

96. Logical issue: `/api/chat` assumes `completion.choices[0]` exists; if the API returns no choices or an empty list, this will raise `IndexError`.[1]

97. Logical issue: `completion.choices[0].message.content` is assumed to be a string; if the API schema changes (for example, content becomes a list of parts), this will break.[1]

98. Logical issue: no logging is implemented beyond a print in `init_db`; debugging production issues is harder without structured logs.[1]

99. Logical issue: database errors during chat handling (insert or update) are not individually caught; if inserting the assistant message fails after generating a response, the API still returns a success response, losing chat history.[1]

100. Logical issue: `/api/chat` sets `"enable_thinking": True` in `chat_template_kwargs`; if the model or endpoint does not support this, the parameter may be ignored or cause errors.[1]

that's all.

```python
import os
import uuid
import base64
import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Optional, List

import pymysql
import bcrypt
import jwt
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Depends, UploadFile, File, Form, Header
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from pydantic import BaseModel
from openai import OpenAI
from exa_py import Exa
from flymyai import client as FlyMyAIClient, FlyMyAIPredictException

app = FastAPI()

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

EXA_API_KEY = os.getenv("EXA_API_KEY")
FLYMYAI_KEY = os.getenv("FLYMYAI_API_KEY")
JWT_SECRET = os.getenv("JWT_SECRET")
DB_HOST = os.getenv("DB_HOST")
DB_PORT = int(os.getenv("DB_PORT", "4000"))
DB_USERNAME = os.getenv("DB_USERNAME")
DB_PASSWORD = os.getenv("DB_PASSWORD")
DB_DATABASE = os.getenv("DB_DATABASE")

openai_client = OpenAI(
    api_key=FRIENDLI_TOKEN,
    base_url="",
)

exa_client = Exa(EXA_API_KEY) if EXA_API_KEY else None
fma_client = FlyMyAIClient(apikey=FLYMYAI_KEY) if FLYMYAI_KEY else None


def get_db():
    connection = pymysql.connect(
        host=DB_HOST,
        port=DB_PORT,
        user=DB_USERNAME,
        password=DB_PASSWORD,
        database=DB_DATABASE,
        ssl={"ssl": {}},
        cursorclass=pymysql.cursors.DictCursor,
    )
    try:
        yield connection
    finally:
        connection.close()


def init_db():
    conn = pymysql.connect(
        host=DB_HOST,
        port=DB_PORT,
        user=DB_USERNAME,
        password=DB_PASSWORD,
        database=DB_DATABASE,
        ssl={"ssl": {}},
        cursorclass=pymysql.cursors.DictCursor,
    )
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
                id VARCHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY,
                username VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
                email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
                password_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
                created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
            )
            """
        )
        cur.execute(
            """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS conversations (
                id VARCHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY,
                user_id VARCHAR(36) NOT NULL,
                title VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'New Chat',
                created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                updated_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
            )
            """
        )
        cur.execute(
            """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (
                id VARCHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY,
                conversation_id VARCHAR(36) NOT NULL,
                role VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
                content TEXT NOT NULL,
                reasoning_content TEXT,
                image_url TEXT,
                exa_sources TEXT,
                created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
            )
            """
        )
        cur.execute(
            """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS uploaded_files (
                id VARCHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY,
                user_id VARCHAR(36) NOT NULL,
                conversation_id VARCHAR(36),
                filename VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
                content_type VARCHAR(100),
                file_data LONGBLOB,
                text_content LONGTEXT,
                created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
            )
            """
        )
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()


try:
    init_db()
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Warning: init_db() failed (tables may already exist): {e}")


def create_token(user_id: str) -> str:
    payload = {
        "user_id": user_id,
        "exp": datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(days=30),
    }
    return jwt.encode(payload, JWT_SECRET, algorithm="HS256")


def decode_token(token: str) -> str:
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(token, JWT_SECRET, algorithms=["HS256"])
        return payload["user_id"]
    except Exception:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid or expired token")


def get_current_user(authorization: Optional[str] = Header(None)) -> str:
    if not authorization or not authorization.startswith("Bearer "):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Not authenticated")
    token = authorization.split(" ", 1)[1]
    return decode_token(token)


class RegisterRequest(BaseModel):
    username: str
    email: str
    password: str


class LoginRequest(BaseModel):
    email: str
    password: str


class ChatRequest(BaseModel):
    conversation_id: Optional[str] = None
    message: str
    use_web_search: bool = False
    generate_image: bool = False
    file_ids: Optional[List[str]] = []


class NewConversationRequest(BaseModel):
    title: Optional[str] = "New Chat"

@app.post("/api/register")
def register(req: RegisterRequest, db=Depends(get_db)):
    user_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    hashed = bcrypt.hashpw(req.password.encode(), bcrypt.gensalt()).decode()
    try:
        with db.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "INSERT INTO users (id, username, email, password_hash) VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s)",
                (user_id, req.username, req.email, hashed),
            )
        db.commit()
    except pymysql.err.IntegrityError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Email or username already exists")
    token = create_token(user_id)
    return {"token": token, "user_id": user_id, "username": req.username}


@app.post("/api/login")
def login(req: LoginRequest, db=Depends(get_db)):
    with db.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = %s", (req.email,))
        user = cur.fetchone()
    if not user or not bcrypt.checkpw(
        req.password.encode(), user["password_hash"].encode()
    ):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid credentials")
    token = create_token(user["id"])
    return {"token": token, "user_id": user["id"], "username": user["username"]}

    news_keywords = [

def build_exa_query_params(message: str):
    now = datetime.utcnow()
    end_date = now.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z")
    start_date = (now - timedelta(days=90)).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z")
    is_recent = any(
        w in message.lower()
        for w in [
            "today",
            "latest",
            "recent",
            "news",
            "ma",
            "friss",
            "legújabb",
            "aktuális",
            "2026",
            "2025",
        ]
    )
    params = {
        "num_results": 100,
        "type": "instant",
        "contents": {
            "summary": {"query": message},
            "extras": {"links": 1},
        },
    }
    if is_recent:
        params["start_crawl_date"] = start_date
        params["end_crawl_date"] = end_date
        params["start_published_date"] = start_date
        params["end_published_date"] = end_date
    return params


def run_exa_search(message: str):
    if exa_client is None:
        return [], []
    params = build_exa_query_params(message)
    result = exa_client.search(message, **params)
    sources = []
    summaries = []
    for r in result.results:
        title = getattr(r, "title", "") or ""
        url = getattr(r, "url", "") or ""
        summary = ""
        if hasattr(r, "summary") and r.summary:
            summary = r.summary
        elif hasattr(r, "text") and r.text:
            summary = r.text[:500]
        if summary:
            summaries.append(f"- {title}: {summary}")
            sources.append({"title": title, "url": url})
    return summaries, sources

def generate_image_from_prompt(prompt: str) -> Optional[str]:
    if fma_client is None:
        return None
    payload = {
        "prompt": prompt,
        "aspect_ratio": None,
        "image_size": None,
        "image": None,
        "image1": None,
        "image2": None,
        "image3": None,
        "image4": None,
        "image5": None,
        "image6": None,
        "image7": None,
        "image8": None,
        "image9": None,
        "image10": None,
        "image11": None,
        "image12": None,
        "image13": None,
    }
    try:
        response = fma_client.predict(model="flymyai/nano-banana-2", payload=payload)
        image_encoded = response.output_data["image"]
        image_bytes = base64.b64decode(image_encoded)
        b64_str = base64.b64encode(image_bytes).decode("utf-8")
        return f"data:image/jpeg;base64,{b64_str}"
    except FlyMyAIPredictException:
        return None


@app.post("/api/chat")
async def chat(
    req: ChatRequest, user_id: str = Depends(get_current_user), db=Depends(get_db)
):
    if not req.conversation_id:
        conv_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        short_title = req.message[:60] if len(req.message) > 60 else req.message
        with db.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "INSERT INTO conversations (id, user_id, title) VALUES (%s, %s, %s)",
                (conv_id, user_id, short_title),
            )
        db.commit()
    else:
        conv_id = req.conversation_id
        with db.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "SELECT id FROM conversations WHERE id = %s AND user_id = %s",
                (conv_id, user_id),
            )
            if not cur.fetchone():
                raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Forbidden")

    with db.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            "SELECT role, content FROM messages WHERE conversation_id = %s ORDER BY created_at ASC",
            (conv_id,),
        )
        history = cur.fetchall()

    file_context = ""
    if req.file_ids:
        for fid in req.file_ids:
            with db.cursor() as cur:
                cur.execute(
                    "SELECT filename, text_content FROM uploaded_files WHERE id = %s AND user_id = %s",
                    (fid, user_id),
                )
                f = cur.fetchone()
            if f and f["text_content"]:
                file_context += (
                    f"\n\n[File: {f['filename']}]\n{f['text_content'][:8000]}"
                )

    exa_sources: List[dict] = []
    exa_context = ""
    use_search = req.use_web_search or should_use_web_search(req.message)
    if use_search:
        summaries, exa_sources = run_exa_search(req.message)
        if summaries:
            exa_context = (
                "\n\nWeb search results (summaries):\n" + "\n".join(summaries[:40])
            )

    is_image_request = req.generate_image or detect_image_request(req.message)
    image_data_url = None
    if is_image_request:
        image_data_url = generate_image_from_prompt(req.message)

    messages_for_llm = []
    messages_for_llm.append(
        {
            "role": "system",
            "content": "You are a helpful, intelligent assistant. Answer in the same language the user writes in. Be concise and accurate.",
        }
    )

    for h in history[-20:]:
        messages_for_llm.append({"role": h["role"], "content": h["content"]})

    user_content = req.message
    if file_context:
        user_content += file_context
    if exa_context:
        user_content += exa_context

    messages_for_llm.append({"role": "user", "content": user_content})

    completion = openai_client.chat.completions.create(
        model="zai-org/GLM-5",
        extra_body={
            "parse_reasoning": True,
            "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": True},
        },
        messages=messages_for_llm,
    )

    assistant_message = completion.choices[0].message
    assistant_content = assistant_message.content
    reasoning = getattr(assistant_message, "reasoning_content", None)

    user_msg_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    assistant_msg_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    exa_sources_json = json.dumps(exa_sources, ensure_ascii=False) if exa_sources else None

    with db.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            "INSERT INTO messages (id, conversation_id, role, content) VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s)",
            (user_msg_id, conv_id, "user", req.message),
        )
        cur.execute(
            "INSERT INTO messages (id, conversation_id, role, content, reasoning_content, image_url, exa_sources) VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)",
            (
                assistant_msg_id,
                conv_id,
                "assistant",
                assistant_content,
                reasoning,
                image_data_url,
                exa_sources_json,
            ),
        )
        cur.execute(
            "UPDATE conversations SET updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = %s",
            (conv_id,),
        )
    db.commit()

    return {
        "conversation_id": conv_id,
        "message_id": assistant_msg_id,
        "content": assistant_content,
        "reasoning_content": reasoning,
        "image_url": image_data_url,
        "exa_sources": exa_sources,
    }
```
